summary: International exchange engineer onboarding: personal Mac reimage, legacy service-account mapping, and temporary escrow
description:
Issue summary:
An incoming international exchange engineer (Nimbus AI program) starts 2026-03-17 in our EU office. They are arriving with a personal MacBook Pro that is currently enrolled in a third-party Jamf MDM tied to their previous employer, and they have several legacy service accounts (prefix `nimbus-`) used for CI and experiment infra that need to be reconciled and migrated to Redwood identities.

Impact:
- Risk of delayed ramp if device cannot be reimaged and enrolled in corporate Jamf within first-day onboarding.
- Legacy service accounts may continue running jobs under old credentials, creating audit and billing gaps.
- KMS key tagging and asset ownership must be set correctly for compliance with EU data residency rules.

Background/context:
- Candidate: Mateo Ruiz (exchange engineer, 3-month placement via Nimbus partnership).
- Nimbus accounts and service principals are still live in shared AWS account `nimbus-data-prod`.
- Nimbus infra uses a set of long-lived service creds (nimbus-ci-01, nimbus-kv-sync) that must be rotated and mapped to newly provisioned Redwood service accounts before Nimbus creds are revoked.
- Mateo intends to use his personal Mac for the placement; HR approved conditional BYOD but requires reimaging to corporate baseline and MDM enrollment.

Requested outcomes / acceptance criteria:
1) Mateo's Mac wiped and reimaged to Redwood standard macOS image, enrolled in corporate Jamf, and bound to SSO + 2FA before first day.
2) All legacy `nimbus-` service accounts identified, a migration plan created, and short-lived Redwood service accounts issued. No long-lived Nimbus credentials should remain active after cutover.
3) KMS key tagging and asset ownership set to `owner:platform-onboarding/mateo.ruiz`, `region:eu-west` and documented for audits.
4) Temporary escrow of specific Nimbus service account credentials for up to 7 days during migration (audit log required); escrow access must be restricted to SRE onboarding rotation.

Steps to complete (high level):
- IT: schedule remote wipe & send reprovisioning instructions; arrange Jamf enrollment slot on 2026-03-16.
- SRE: enumerate running CI jobs using `nimbus-ci-*` principals (query CI dashboard & ARNs).
- Security: create timebound KMS policy and a temporary vault path for escrowed creds; ensure HSM-backed key usage where required.
- IAM: create new Redwood service principals, attach least-privilege policies, and prepare rotation playbook.
- Legal/HR: confirm BYOD paperwork and device-acceptance form have been signed and attached to the employee record.

Notes on constraints/risks:
- Mateo is flying in on 2026-03-16 and wants to start 2026-03-17; tight timeline for reimage + credential cutover.
- Nimbus org ownership disputes: one Nimbus admin (slack @nimbus-admin) has flagged objections to bulk credential rotation until migration plan is present.
- Network access: Mateo will need VPN split-tunnel exceptions for on-prem legacy infra during migration window.

Attachments / links:
- Slack thread: #onboarding (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C09ONBOARD) (see thread ts 2026-03-11 09:12)
- Confluence runbook: "Onboarding BYOD reimage & Jamf enroll" (confluence.redwood.company/display/Onboard/BYOD-Reimage)

investigation_notes: Initial scan (2026-03-13) found 4 active ARNs using nimbus-ci-01 in CI runner tags.
No production customer data appears to be directly accessed by those CI jobs; primarily build artifacts and internal test buckets.
Jamf enrollment fails if device has an existing MDM profile tied to another org — remote wipe required.
BYOD policy requires device-level FileVault enabled and MDM enforced before provisioning elevated tokens.
KMS keys used by nimbus-kv-sync are HSM-backed; rotation must be co-ordinated with Security to avoid data-access outages.
